newsitem.title: USA: Ex-brokers to surrender to Escambia Cty next week.
newsitem.headline: Ex-brokers to surrender to Escambia Cty next week.

text.p: Four brokers are expected to surrender by the middle of next week to face racketeering charges stemming from the sale of derivative securities to the former Escambia County, Fla., comptroller a prosecutor said Wednesday.

Florida prosecutors filed charges Oct 16 against Kent Tippets Black, Joel Lee Hurst, David Eric Lynch and Larry Eugene Muller, all of whom formerly worked in the Houston office of First Montauk Securities Corp.
Escambia County State Attorney Russell Edgar said he had spoken to attorneys for all four and expected them to surrender for arraignment "probably toward the middle of the week."
He added, "If they don't, we'll go get 'em."
He said all were expected to enter not guilty pleas, and none were involved in discussions concerning potential plea agreements.

The charges allege that the four schemed to defraud Escambia County by selling former county comptroller Joseph Flowers unsuitably risky mortgage-backed securities, by inflating the prices of the securities and by lying about the liquidity and risk involved.
The county invested $45 million in derivative securites between 1990 and 1994, and saw the value of its portfolio drop by half in late 1994.

The securities were finally sold at a $15 million loss last year. Because the securities were bought with tax revenues needed for short-term expenses, the county was forced to borrow money and cancel some capital projects.
The brokers were let go from First Montauk due to market conditions and before the allegations of irregular trading arose, First Montauk's general counsel, Robert Rabinowitz, said.
The firm's principals had no knowledge of the transactions, Rabinowitz said.
The Red Bank, N.J.-based firm agreed to pay the county $900,000 in March to settle a civl lawsuit filed against it by Escambia County.
